children: According to Yonhap, RTHK and the Hong Kong Economic Times, most Asian equity markets opened firmer on Tuesday, tracking a strong Wall Street session in which the Nasdaq set a record close and chip stocks rallied.

Tokyo's cash equity market was closed for a Japanese public holiday, a citizens' bridge day between Respect for the Aged Day and the Autumnal Equinox, so no cash-session prices were set for the Nikkei 225 or TOPIX.

Seoul's KOSPI opened sharply higher, rising 153.89 points to 7,161.61 and climbing back above the 7,100 mark, up more than 2% in early trade. Chipmakers led the advance, with Samsung Electronics up about 2.0% and SK Hynix gaining around 2.6%.

Hong Kong stocks opened higher, with the Hang Seng Index up 128 points at 25,170. Tencent rose about 3% and Alibaba added around 2% in early dealings, while MINIMAX climbed more than 5%. Xiaomi edged up about 1.5%.

Taiwan's TAIEX opened up 262.2 points at 47,981.04 and then surged as much as 882 points to an intraday record of 48,601, led by the tech sector. TSMC gained around 0.6% and MediaTek jumped more than 8%, while chip-IP designer Aspeed hit its daily limit at NT$21,800, a record price for a Taiwan-listed share.

In mainland China, the four main indexes opened higher together, with more than 3,100 stocks advancing; storage, GPU and HBM names led. The Shanghai Composite rose nearly 0.2% in early trade and the ChiNext Index gained more than 1%.

title: ASIA MARKET OPEN | Seoul's KOSPI Opens Up Over 2% Above 7,100, Taiwan Sets Record High; Tokyo Shut for Holiday
